prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map captures the 3D layout from the foreground round table and nearby standing people (brightest, ~0.4–1.0 m away and within the camera wearer's arm's reach) to the seated man in blue (~1.2–2.5 m away in the middle ground) and the pastry display case, beverage cooler, and back-left counter (darkest, ~2.5–5.0 m away). In Frames 1 and 2, two standing people flank the left (yellow shirt) and right (black shirt) edges at ~0.5–0.8 m while occluding the background, before the right-side person exits and the wearer approaches the seated man in Frames 3–4 (brightening his silhouette from ~2.5 m to ~1.2 m) and retreats in Frame 5 (~2.2 m). In Frames 3 and 4, the depth layers clearly separate the foreground yellow-shirted torso on the left (~0.5 m, within arm's reach) from the white-shirted person standing ~0.5–1.0 m directly behind/ahead of them (~1.5–2.0 m from the wearer, facing away toward the back counter) and ~1.5 m left of the seated man facing the wearer. This map clarifies continuous metric distance ordering and foreground-background separation—such as the exact shelf recession inside the pastry case and the depth gap between overlapping standing figures—that motion blur and flat lighting obscure in RGB alone. However, it is unreliable in motion-blurred Frames 2 and 5 where the table items and seated man's head/cup smear into indistinct blobs, and on the glass cooler doors which appear artificially flat instead of showing interior depth.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates discrete person and object instances against the unlabelled room background, identifying the seated man in blue (~1.2–2.5 m away on the right, facing toward the camera wearer) and the close standing people (~0.4–2.0 m away on the left and right edges) across the sequence. In Frame 1, it segments the yellow-shirted person cropped on the left (~0.6 m), the black-shirted person cropped on the right (~0.5 m, within arm's reach), and the seated man between them (~2.5 m); in Frames 3 and 4, as the wearer moves closer, it resolves the occlusion on the left by separating the yellow-shirted person (~0.5 m) from the white-shirted person standing just ahead of them (~1.5–2.0 m away, facing away) into distinct masks, including splitting the white-shirted person's torso and legs around the occluding shoulder in Frame 3. It also detects small held or background objects within arm's reach of the people—specifically the cup held in the seated man's right hand near his lap in Frames 3 and 4 (~1.2–1.8 m from the wearer) and a bottle on the back counter in Frame 4 (~3.5 m away)—before the wearer turns and retreats in Frame 5. Compared to RGB, the instance masks sharply delineate overlapping body boundaries between the tightly spaced standing people in Frames 3 and 4. However, the map is unreliable during heavy motion blur in Frame 2 (missing the seated man in blue and the left-side person entirely and fragmenting the right-side person into two 'person' masks), misses the foreground table and its items (bag, bottles, cans) within the wearer's reach across all frames, and misclassifies a pastry inside the display case behind the seated man as a 'donut' in Frame 4.
descriptions.pose: The pose map tracks the 2D upper-body and leg keypoints (yellow) and hand keypoints (magenta) SOLELY for the seated man in the blue shirt (~1.2–2.5 m away in front of the cooler/display case), while omitting all other people and objects in the room. Across Frames 1, 3, 4, and 5, the symmetrically spread shoulder keypoints and facial cluster (eyes, nose, ears) show his torso and head facing toward the camera wearer and foreground table, angled slightly to the left, with his head keypoints tilting downward toward the table in Frames 3 and 4 as the wearer approaches from ~2.5 m to ~1.2 m. The arm keypoints track his right hand within his own arm's reach as it moves from near his face while drinking in Frame 1, down to his right knee holding the cup near the foreground table in Frames 3 and 4 (where a magenta hand cluster is detected on his left hand resting on his left thigh, ~1.2 m from the wearer), and back up to his face in Frame 5 as the wearer retreats. This skeletal wireframe reveals exact joint angles, seated hip-to-knee posture, and head orientation even when dark sunglasses and shadows obscure his eyes and lap in the RGB images. However, the map is unreliable in Frame 1 where the torso and left arm are incomplete, fails completely in motion-blurred Frame 2 where no skeleton is detected, misses his right hand's magenta finger keypoints while holding the cup, and fails to detect the close standing people (~0.4–2.0 m away on the left and right edges) whose heads or bodies are partially out of view or facing away.
